Base directory for this skill: /Users/rod/build/stopwatch-screensaver/.claude/skills/port-hack

# Porting an xscreensaver hack

The rules live in `AGENTS.md` ("Rules", "Gotchas") and the path-scoped notes in
`.claude/rules/`. This skill sets the order of work and the points to stop. The
numbered steps are in `adding-a-hack.md` and the recipes it names are in
`techniques.md`, both next to this file. For several hacks in one go, read
`batches.md` too.

## 1. Pick, then read the source

Before copying anything, read `techniques.md` and every file in
`.claude/rules/` (`hacks.md`, `x11shim.md`, `device-display.md`, `gl.md`,
`tools-scoring.md`) in full. The gotchas live there, and a harness may not load
them for you (`.pi/rules` links to the same directory for pi).

Take S-rated rows from `docs/porting-assessment.md` first, and prefer a low
**Speed** band: the table runs each unported S hack on the host. The effort
rating counts missing shim calls, not memory, speed or stack (Braid was S, and
would have shown as high). A high band is a hack that will probably run slowly
on the board; a low band is not a guarantee, because a hack still doing
software `double` maths runs far slower on the device than on the host. Read
the hack's source before copying it, and look for:

| The source has | Technique (seen in) |
| --- | --- |
| Arrays or a state over a few MB | Build-time patch (Maze) |
| `sin`, `cos`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `double` in a hot loop | Single precision (Galaxy, Substrate) |
| Locals over a few KB | Stack check (Rorschach) |
| An allocation of 100 KB or more, or `exit()` on failure | Large allocations (Substrate) |
| Pixmaps, clip masks, a logo image | Images (Maze) |
| A hack that restarts itself | Restart leak test (Maze, Substrate) |
| A `free` that relies on state `draw` sets up (a lazy `initted`) | Stopping before the first draw (Blaster) |
| Hairlines, fades or `glPolygonOffset` in a GL hack | Thin lines in a GL hack |
| Xft text (`XftDrawStringUtf8`) | Xft text (XJack) |
| Threads, shared memory | Skipping a hack |
| A licence header | Read it; add a notices section only if it differs from jwz's |

## 2. Set up

Work in a worktree off `origin/main`. Its setup and the commands it refuses are
in "Worktree setup".

## 3. Red, copy, green

Follow `adding-a-hack.md`. Show the registry test failing before
copying. Fill each shim gap test-first, then break the code on purpose and
watch the test fail ("Tests that cannot be fooled"). Filling a missing
function is a shim gap. Changing what every hack sees (the runner, a default, a
shared helper) is not: stop and ask Rod first. A speed-up in the shared GL
layer counts too, even when every pinned frame hash still matches (HexTrail's
deferred depth clear): ask before writing it, and name it in the PR body.

## 4. Verify on the host

Run `pio test -e native`, `uv run --with pytest --with pillow pytest tools/tests`
and `uv run tools/check_notices.py`, and dump frames at several counts. For a
single-precision wrapper, also build for the device and run
`uv run tools/softdouble_report.py <name>`: a count in a per-frame function is
a literal, macro or struct the rename missed (`techniques.md`). Host
frames cannot show a byte swap, which happens in the push to the display: judge
colour on the device, on a colour you know the answer to.

## 5. Device

Flash only after Rod says so in this conversation; approval for one flash is
not approval for the next. See "Device capture". Report "compiles", "host tests
pass" and "runs on the device" separately; only Rod can say what the screen
shows. If it is slow, measure, change one thing, flash again and compare; if it
is still slow, say so and suggest dropping it. A hack that runs at a good rate
can still go: Rod dropped Boing (8.3 fps, "pretty boring on a small screen")
and asked for HexTrail to be tuned because it fell under 10 fps before the
rotation moved on. Judge a hack on a 466 px round screen, and by its worst
window as well as its mean. Record the numbers in
`tools/assessment_measured.md.in`, marking anything unmeasured as such. After a
batch, log one 20 s-a-hack rotation lap and run `tools/triage_hacks.py`
(`hacks.md` says how): it shows which hacks are step-bound, push-bound or paced
by their own delay, with their soft-double calls, so a slow hack is looked at
for the right reason.

## 6. Deliver

Commit named paths. Open the draft PR with `entire trail create` and put what
is unverified in its body. After a rebase, a push needs `--force-with-lease`:
ask Rod each time. Rod approves and merges; then delete the branch and
fast-forward `main`. New gotchas go in the matching `.claude/rules/` file (or
`AGENTS.md` if they apply everywhere) in the same PR, and deferred
ideas become issues.

## Done means

A port is done on the host only when all of these hold: a dumped frame viewed
at two or more frame counts (with seeds forced if the hack picks a mode); a
leak test, mutation-checked; the largest stack frame measured; the hash pinned
from a frame you looked at; and a notices row that matches each file's header.

## Red flags

| Thought | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "It is rated S, so I need not read it" | Maze was rated L for Xlib gaps; the real blocker was a 20 MB `calloc`. |
| "It compiles, so it works" | Rorschach compiled and rebooted on its first frame. |
| "The colours look right" | Not from a host frame: every hack was byte swapped until Maze. |
| "My test passes, so it tests something" | A test through Pyro passed with the runner broken. Break the code on purpose. |
| "AGENTS.md says to fix shim gaps, so I can change the runner" | A new function is a gap. A change every hack sees needs Rod. |
| "Rod approved flashing earlier" | Ask again for each flash. |
| "Single precision is done, so the hack is as fast as it gets" | HexTrail gained 0.3 fps from it and 2.3 from a depth clear in the GL layer. Read what the shared code does each frame. |
| "The mean is above 10 fps" | HexTrail's mean was 15.3 and its worst window 10.8; its step grew all cycle. Read the lowest window. |
| "Dump with 0 and 5 frames exits cleanly, so it works" | That shows it starts and stops, not what it draws. Convert a frame to PNG and look. |
| "A `0` in `kBaseline` keeps the suite green" | It also stops the suite checking a single frame. Use `0x1ull` until you have looked, then pin. |
| "A hook will not run, so `--no-verify`" | That skips ruff, markdownlint and gitleaks. `SKIP=<hook>`, and say so in the PR. |

6	hack, and holds a recipe per trap. The steps:
7	
8	1. Check its row in `docs/porting-assessment.md` (effort and Speed band) and
9	   read its licence header.
10	2. Update the expected list in `firmware/test/test_hacks/test_hacks.c` and see
11	   it fail. Add `test_<name>_stops_do_not_leak` beside the others, and
12	   mutation-check it: remove each free a wrapper adds and watch it fail.
13	3. Copy the file to `firmware/src/hacks/<name>/<name>.c`, add the notices row
14	   and an `extern` plus entry in `hacks/registry.c`.
15	4. Fill shim gaps test-first in `firmware/test/test_xshim/`. The compile
16	   check in `score_hacks.py` shows what is missing.
17	5. Host tests pass, dump a frame and look at it, then (with Rod's go-ahead)
18	   flash and measure fps and free heap/PSRAM over serial. To pin its frame
19	   hash after looking at the frame, put `0x1ull` in `kBaseline`, run
20	   `pio test -e native -f test_hacks`, convert the "Was N" in the failure line
21	   with `python3 -c "print(hex(N))"`, and run it again. A new hack never gets
22	   `0` in `kBaseline`: `0` is for a hack left unpinned on purpose, with the
23	   reason in its comment (DecayScreen, RotZoomer).
24	6. Regenerate the assessment and add measurements to
25	   `tools/assessment_measured.md.in`, then re-run the speed backtest: each port
26	   adds a point to the check of the Speed bands, which were fitted to the first
27	   29 hacks. To make a port a real test, commit its host time and predicted
28	   range first (`docs/speed-predictions.md` shows the form), flash it as copied,
29	   and add its name to `HOLDOUT` in `tools/speed_backtest.py`. The first four
30	   (Mountain, Epicycle, Kaleidescope, Celtic) all fell where predicted.
31	7. If a hack is slow and `double`-heavy (many `double`s, `sqrt`, `sin`/`cos`,
32	   `pow`), try a single-precision wrapper like `hacks/galaxy_single.c` (for a
33	   plain screenhack, `hacks/substrate_single.c`; the recipe is in the skill's
34	   `techniques.md`), and compare double and float frames at several frame
35	   counts. A resource
36	   override can skip a hack's restart cleanup: Galaxy leaked at `count: 2`, so
37	   leak-test any override.
38	8. If Rod drops a port after seeing it (Hypnowheel, Boing; Celtic was dropped

40	   from `g_hacks[]`, the expected list, its hash and its leak test; keep the
41	   source and notices row; add `name: reason` (short: it is printed as a

48	   Unhook its build steps too: its entry in `patch_float_literals.py` and any
49	   pre-script only it needs (BlockTube's `gl_textures.py`), or every build

1	# Porting techniques
2	
3	Recipes for the traps listed in `SKILL.md`. Each says when it applies, what to
4	do, and what it did the last time.
5	
6	## Build-time patch
7	
8	When: the hack's own constants make it too big for the board. Maze keeps a
9	1000 by 1000 maze and three 1,000,000-entry move lists in one `calloc`, about
10	20 MB, and the board has 8 MB of PSRAM.
11	
12	- The copy in `hacks/<name>/` stays byte-identical to upstream (`cmp` it).
13	- A PlatformIO `pre:` script (`firmware/patch_maze.py`) writes a patched copy
14	  into the build directory, using a tested function (`tools/maze_patch.py`)
15	  that raises if upstream's lines change. A wrapper (`hacks/maze_small.c`)
16	  includes that copy, and the original is excluded in `build_src_filter` of
17	  all three environments (`stopwatch`, `native`, `dump`).
18	- Maze's limits went from 1000 to 80: about 125 KB.
19	- A patch can switch off a branch (Pacman's `NRAND (2) == 0` becomes `0`) or
20	  replace a whole function (its route search becomes a loop). Check the
21	  original's SHA-256 so an upstream edit fails the build. Before a rewrite, pin
22	  a long-run fingerprint taken with the original (30,000 frames, every ghost's
23	  position every 100), show the code ran, and mutate the order to watch the pin
24	  fail.
25	
26	## Single precision
27	
28	When: a hot loop does `double` maths or calls `sin`, `cos`, `sqrt` or `pow`.
29	The ESP32-S3 has a single-precision FPU only, so double runs in software.
30	
31	- Find the hot loop first and count the calls. Substrate makes four `sin` calls
32	  per sand grain, with 64 grains a crack and up to 100 cracks: about 25,000
33	  software `sin`s a frame. Its step grew from 5 ms to 121 ms as the picture
34	  filled.
35	- Wrapper `hacks/<name>_single.c`: include the framework headers first, then
36	  `hacks/single_precision.h`, then the unmodified hack. Exclude the original in
37	  `build_src_filter` of all three environments.
38	- `M_PI` is a double literal, so the angle arithmetic stays double: put
39	  `#undef M_PI` and a float definition after the header. Literals such as
40	  `0.81` stay double too, and a header cannot change them: `0.5 * x` with a
41	  float `x` is software double maths. Check the wrapper's object for soft-double
42	  helpers with `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm braid.o | grep ' U __.*df'` (compile with
43	  `-Os -mlongcalls` and the shim's include paths). If any remain, rewrite the
44	  literals at build time as Braid does: `tools/float_literals.py` (tested, skips
45	  strings and comments) run by `firmware/patch_float_literals.py`, and the
46	  wrapper includes `<name>_floatlit.c` from the build directory. GCC's
47	  `-fsingle-precision-constant` does the same, but Apple clang ignores it, so
48	  host tests would run other arithmetic than the board.
49	- Galaxy, Drift, Discrete, Flame and Substrate were wrapped before this check
50	  and now go through it too, with `single_constants.h` (`MAXRAND`, `M_PI`) and
51	  `single_frand.h`. Run `uv run tools/softdouble_report.py <name>` on the
52	  wrapper's object after `pio run -e stopwatch`: any count in a per-frame
53	  function means a literal, macro or `double` struct field the rename missed
54	  (`x11shim.md` has the four that did). A trig argument that is a big whole
55	  number is a fifth: look at a frame before trusting the float build.
56	- A plain single-precision wrapper is cheap to try: include
57	  `single_precision.h`, `single_constants.h` and `<name>_floatlit.c`, exclude
58	  the original in the three `build_src_filter` lines and list the name in
59	  `patch_float_literals.py`. Measure it on the board and drop it if it moves
60	  nothing. On the board, step before to after: Hopalong 7-20 to 3.4 ms,
61	  WhirlWindWarp 6-26 to 3.8 ms, BinaryHorizon 95.8 to 31.8 ms, Barcode 77.1 to
62	  56.1 ms (frames byte-identical), XSpirograph 44.2 to 10.9 ms, Vines 182 to
63	  10.3 ms; Bouboule stayed at 14.5 ms.
64	- Hand-written `sin` and `cos` (`hacks/fast_trig.h`) moved Braid by 5%. Do the
65	  literals first.
66	- Compare double and float frames at several counts. Early frames match; a
67	  chaotic hack diverges later but should keep its look.
68	- GL hacks too: Hypnowheel's spiral called `cos` and `sin` in `double` for
69	  every vertex, about 275 ms of a 706 ms step, hidden behind a fill-heavy look.
70	  Its wrapper (`hypnowheel_single_gl.c`) adapts `get_position` and
71	  `get_rotation` as HexTrail's does.
72	- Results: Galaxy 5 to 14 fps. Substrate step 119-121 ms to 37-38 ms, 6.2 to
73	  12.5 fps.
74	- A hack that passes the address of its own `double` local to a shim function
75	  (`rgb_to_hsv (..., &s, &v)`) writes eight bytes into a four-byte float, and
76	  the compiler does not warn. Moire's frames were all different from the
77	  double build's until `moire_single.c` mapped the call to an adapter defined
78	  before `single_precision.h`. Cmp the wrapper's frames against the unmodified
79	  hack's. A hack with no decimal literals must stay out of
80	  `patch_float_literals.py`, which refuses it.
81	- Once the maths is float, look at the fills before the next idea. CWaves'
82	  cosines were 4 ms of a 61 ms step; its 233 column fills were 57 (a thin
83	  full-height rectangle touches a new cache line a store). See `hacks.md`.
84	- A float build can break a check that held in double. Both the S3 (`madd.s`)
85	  and arm64 fuse a multiply and an add, so `t*n - floor(t*n)` uses the exact
86	  product for the subtraction and the rounded one for the `floor`, and can
87	  come out slightly negative: Celtic's `assert(tt>=0 && tt<1)` aborted at
88	  t 0.331093 with 3422 segments. The 3000-frame test (`pio test`) found it
89	  on the host, and the same abort would have hit the board. Compute the
90	  product once in a build-time patch (`tools/celtic_patch.py`). Map any libm
91	  call the hack makes that `single_precision.h` does not (`rint`, `floor`),
92	  and check the object with `nm` for `__*df*` helpers, not only `__muldf3`.
93	
94	## Slow hack
95	
96	When: a ported hack runs under about 10 fps and the push is not the cause
97	(`step` in the serial line is large).
98	
99	- For a GL hack, flash a `-DGL_PROFILE` build first (AGENTS.md): it splits
100	  the frame into stages, and time in none of them is the hack's own code.
101	  Issue #73 guessed Hypnowheel was 70 percent blended fill; the profile showed
102	  a third of its frame was `double` trig.
103	- A worst-case microbenchmark is not the workload. A PSRAM cache miss costs
104	  about 220 cycles, which suggested GL fill was memory-bound; a banded renderer
105	  in internal RAM, built on that, was exact and slower (neighbouring triangles
106	  share cache lines). A/B the first working slice of a speed idea on the board
107	  before building the rest, and stop if it does not pay.
108	- Do not trust a host profile (`sample` on the dump program) for where the
109	  time goes. A Mac does `double` at full speed, so software-double code looks
110	  cheap there: Braid's disc fill was 6% on the host and the largest cost on the
111	  board.
112	- Split the step on the device with a temporary build flag that makes the
113	  expensive call return at once (Braid: `XDrawLine`). The step left is the
114	  hack's own cost; the difference is the drawing. Remove the flag before
115	  committing.
116	- Count what is called per frame (segments, calls, rows) before guessing,
117	  and look at the object file for soft-double helpers (see "Single precision").
118	- Change one thing, pin that the pixels did not move (`cmp` frames at several
119	  counts, or the pinned hash), flash, and compare second windows. Braid's four
120	  changes were worth 2.7-3.2 times, 1.05, and 1.3.
121	- Wide lines (`line_width` above 1) are the costly path: a quad filled a row at
122	  a time, plus two discs for round caps. `stroke.c` keeps a table of disc rows
123	  by width up to 16. A wide full circle through `XDrawArc` is about a thousand
124	  such segments (Deluxe: 94% of a frame, 2-5 fps); `stroke_circle` fills it as
125	  a ring in two spans a row.
126	- When the cost is overpaint, not `double` maths, a host split does find the
127	  dominant call: `#define XDrawArc(...) 0` in the wrapper, `pio run -e dump`,
128	  then `/usr/bin/time -p .pio/build/dump/program <index> 400 out.raw` three
129	  times, against the baseline. It cannot see costs that live in memory
130	  traffic (Deluxe's alpha mask: nothing on the host, 3-5 ms on the board).
131	- Counting works where timing misleads: a scratch copy of the hack with a
132	  counter in the inner function and a macro round `XDrawLine` gave Celtic's
133	  spline evaluations and line draws per draw call on the host, by graph type.
134	  A cost per eval and per line fitted to a first device capture (about 1.7 us
135	  and 22 us, from three graph types and a handful of windows) estimated 63 ms
136	  for the biggest type after the change; the next capture's 12.6-76.8 ms did
137	  not contradict it, but the log does not say which type each window was, so
138	  the fit is unchecked.
139	- A hack's own pacing constants can be the lever: Celtic's 0.0001 tick (a
140	  patch scales it, `CELTIC_STEP_SCALE`) set both the look-ahead's work and how
141	  many draw calls a picture takes. Count the draw calls a picture takes and
142	  the pause after it before reading `fps=`: with a 5 s pause the column read
143	  5.2 in every window and measured the pause, not the drawing. Use
144	  `1000 / (step + push + delay)` for the drawing rate.
145	- Heap and speed were two problems in Celtic and one fix cured only the
146	  first: the graph sized to the screen cut a pattern's heap about 9 times and
147	  left spline evaluations per call unchanged. Measure both after each change.
148	- A hack that redraws its whole picture every frame to animate colour (Braid)
149	  costs its full draw each frame whatever the push does. Check this before
150	  porting; the scorer does not flag it yet.
151	- A fix that moves the frame rate by under 5% shows the maths was not the
152	  cost. HexTrail in single precision went from 12.7 to 13.0 fps; the 2.3 fps
153	  that mattered came from reading what the GL layer does each frame
154	  (`glshim_clear`) and finding a depth clear that nothing read, because the hack
155	  never enables the depth test. Run `nm` on the object, then read the shared
156	  code the hack calls before trying a third idea in the hack.
157	- A step that grows over the hack's cycle (HexTrail: 19 ms to a ceiling, then it
158	  restarts) needs the worst window, not the mean. Capture at least one full
159	  cycle (150 s covered HexTrail's 65 s), read the lowest `fps=`, and compare the
160	  time spent below 10 fps with the rotation interval: Rod saw it fall under 10
161	  before the 25 s change. If a resource such as `count` scales the cost, give it
162	  an `#ifndef` default in `registry.c` (`HEXTRAIL_COUNT`) so one flash tests
163	  another value, and measure two or three values: count 6 gave a mean of 12.7,
164	  10 gave 9.1 and 20 gave 5.7, in double precision.
165	- Before writing a speed override, grep the hack's header and glue for the
166	  author's own knob (`GLB_SLOW_GL` in `bubble3d.h`, set from the wrapper with
167	  `#undef` and `#define` after the header). It keeps the copy byte-identical
168	  and is the trade the author intended: Bubble3D went from 4-5 fps to a mean
169	  of 11.4. A hack split over several files (entry point in one, work in
170	  another) gets one `<name>_*gl.c` wrapper per file, and only the file that
171	  does the maths needs `single_precision.h`.
172	
173	## Thin lines in a GL hack
174	
175	When: a GL hack draws hairlines or fades (Unknown Pleasures) and looks right
176	in a host frame but flickers on the board. Work down this list, one layer at a
177	time, and look at the screen (or film) after each; each layer hid the next.
178	
179	- Lines hop. TinyGL snaps every vertex to a whole pixel, so a drifting line
180	  jumps. `tinygl_patch.py` keeps the fractional position and draws a Wu line
181	  when the hack enables `GL_LINE_SMOOTH`. Triangles are still snapped.
182	- Quads that hide the lines behind them hide nothing, or the picture is
183	  speckled grey. TinyGL's blend adds colours, ignores alpha and misreads our
184	  byte-swapped pixels, so `SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA` is drawn as an
185	  opaque fill. Smooth lines carry no alpha, so a hack's per-line fade is lost.
186	- A line drawn on its own polygon's edge is erased in dashes: `glPolygonOffset`
187	  was stored and never read. The patch applies it, plus a margin for the
188	  vertex snapping. Check the effect on the host by the second difference of a
189	  frame's total brightness while the picture drifts a fraction of a pixel; change
190	  one thing at a time, because blending once made the experiment unable to
191	  show any effect.
192	- Pieces of a line vanish for one refresh. The panel scans while the push
193	  writes, so a seam crosses the picture. Set `sync_to_refresh` on the hack
194	  (`XLOCKMORE_HACK_SYNCED`); see `.claude/rules/device-display.md` for the
195	  offset, why it is only valid for a full-frame push, and how to film the
196	  result. Cost: up to a refresh of latency a frame, so only a hack that needs
197	  it should ask.
198	- Budget with `gl_budget.py` but expect it to be off: it has no blend term
199	  (Unknown Pleasures was predicted at 251 ms and ran at 267, then 197 once the
200	  fills were opaque). Add the measured row as a calibration point.
201	- After all that a dimming of about 14% for 25 ms at each push remained (issue
202	  #68). Do not promise a hack is flicker-free from a host frame or from the
203	  absence of vanishing lines alone.
204	
205	## Stack check
206	
207	When: locals over a few KB. Compile the hack with `-O1 -fstack-usage` (flags in
208	AGENTS.md) and keep each frame well under the 16 KB loop stack. Host tests
209	cannot see an overflow: Rorschach's 9.6 KB array rebooted the device on its
210	first frame, and only the serial log's "Stack canary" showed it.
211	
212	Recursion: replay it, don't guess. Run the hack on a pthread with a painted
213	1 MB stack over several seeds and thousands of frames (Pacman's generator: 236
214	KB median, 315 KB worst; `ulimit -s` saw only the first, shallow level). Read a
215	frame's size from the ELF (`xtensa-esp32s3-elf-objdump -d`, `entry a1, N`), and
216	decode a panic backtrace with `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-addr2line` against an ELF
217	rebuilt with the same flags. A recursion over a grid is bounded by its cells:
218	replay it from every start.
219	
220	## Large allocations
221	
222	When: one allocation of 100 KB or more, or the hack calls `exit()` if it fails.
223	
224	- `unsigned long` is 4 bytes on the device and 8 on the host, so host leak
225	  numbers are double the device's.
226	- Plain `malloc` and `realloc` of two 868 KB buffers (Substrate) landed in
227	  PSRAM: free PSRAM fell by 1,742,096 bytes, which is 2 x 466 x 466 x 4 plus a
228	  few KB. Internal heap barely moved.
229	- On restart the buffers were freed and allocated again, and free PSRAM
230	  returned to the same value. Read heap and PSRAM in the log to confirm this
231	  for each large hack.
232	
233	## Images
234	
235	Colour pixmaps are canvases: every drawing primitive, `XCopyArea` and
236	`XCopyPlane` draw into them. Bitmaps take only `XCopyArea` from another
237	bitmap. There is no PNG
238	decoder: `image_data_to_pixmap` reads a raw RGB565 blob and
239	mask (format in `ximage-loader.h`), made by `tools/make_logo_blob.py`.
240	`XS_LOGO=<image>` (relative to the repository root) swaps the logo for a local
241	image at build time. Keep a third-party logo under `vendor/`, out of git.
242	
243	A big blob (Pacman's is 3 MB as C text) is built from `vendor/` by a `pre:`
244	script and never committed; write it to a `.partial` file and rename it.
245	
246	## Pixmap double buffering
247	
248	When: a plain screenhack makes two pixmaps, draws into them and `XCopyArea`s the
249	result to the window (Anemone, Anemotaxis, Compass, FuzzyFlakes, Halftone,
250	Interaggregate, LMorph, Wormhole). Since #61 this works as copied, but a back
251	buffer costs 434 KB of PSRAM and a full-frame copy each frame, and dirties
252	every row, so the push loses what the dirty rectangle (#52) saves. Draw
253	straight on the canvas instead, as below. (These eight were ported before #61,
254	when the copy from a blank pixmap erased the picture.)
255	
256	- A pinned hash of a blank frame passes silently (`0xa4f79500bd791711ull`, which
257	  is also Pedal's at frame 200). Look at the frame before pinning.
258	- Upstream switches the buffering off under `HAVE_JWXYZ` ("Don't second-guess
259	  Quartz's double-buffering"), or reads a `doubleBuffer` resource. Write
260	  `hacks/<name>_direct.c`: include `screenhack.h` and the math headers, empty
261	  `XSCREENSAVER_MODULE`, `#define HAVE_JWXYZ`, include the unmodified hack and
262	  register its `HackEntry`. Exclude the original from `build_src_filter` in all
263	  three environments. `grep HAVE_JWXYZ` first: Interaggregate also uses it for
264	  pixel packing, but only in the 24 and 32 bit cases, and the canvas is 16 bit.
265	- A hack that uses a pixmap as storage needs no wrapper. Truchet draws a canvas
266	  bigger than the window into an 866 by 866 pixmap (1.5 MB of PSRAM) and
267	  scrolls it with `XCopyArea` offsets.
268	
269	## Restart leak test
270	
271	When: the hack restarts itself. Override its cycle resource in the test (for
272	example `*maxCycles: 3`), compare `__sanitizer_get_current_allocated_bytes()`
273	before and after many restarts, and prove the test sees a leak by removing a
274	`free` in a temporary copy or leaking from a shim function. Never leave the
275	hack changed: `cmp` it afterwards.
276	
277	Measure the growth first, then set the tolerance just above it (Pacman: exactly
278	0, so 512 bytes). A loose one passes a leaked GC; mutation-check by leaking one.
279	
280	On the device, work out how long a restart takes: cycles times the frame time.
281	Substrate's 10,000 cycles at about 160 ms is 27 minutes, and the restart showed
282	at about 25. Capture that long, with `-DROTATE_SECONDS=0`.
283	
284	## Stopping before the first draw
285	
286	When: the hack allocates on its first `draw` (look for a lazy `initted` flag)
287	but sizes its `free` from values set in `init`. Two quick button presses, or a
288	press with the 90 s rotation, free a hack before it has drawn once. Blaster
289	sets `NUM_ROBOTS` in init, allocates `robots` in draw, and its free loops over
290	`robots[i].lasers`, so freeing it first dereferenced NULL. The dump tool with 0
291	frames exited 139.
292	
293	- `test_every_hack_can_be_stopped_before_its_first_frame` starts and stops every
294	  hack with no frame, so a new port that has this problem fails the host suite.
295	- To fix it without editing the hack, write a wrapper that includes the
296	  unmodified source with `XSCREENSAVER_MODULE` emptied and registers the hack
297	  itself, with a `free` that makes the loop safe (`hacks/blaster_safe.c`).
298	- A real press is rarely handled in that window: Rod's presses on the device
299	  all landed after the first step. Rely on the test, not on pressing buttons.
300	- An xlockmore hack cannot be re-registered that way: `xlockmore.h` has no
301	  include guard, so the hack's own include redefines `XSCREENSAVER_MODULE`
302	  after the wrapper empties it. Swap the callback in the table instead, from a
303	  constructor: `<name>_xlockmore_function_table.hack_init = my_init;`
304	  (`loop_direct.c`, `hypnowheel_single_gl.c`).
305	
306	## Tests that cannot be fooled
307	
308	A test that runs a real hack can pass for the wrong reason. Pyro clears its own
309	window in `init`, so a "starts black" test through Pyro passed with the runner
310	deliberately broken. Test shared runner behaviour with stub hacks
311	(`test_runner_xsft.c`) and mutate the code to see the test fail.
312	
313	A check can also be true before the hack has run. "At least 20 non-black
314	pixels" proved a hack drew, until Substrate started on a white canvas and
315	passed without drawing at all. Compare with the canvas as the hack started, and
316	keep a stub hack that draws nothing, on the colour that fooled the old check, to
317	show the test can fail. When a change alters what every hack starts with (the
318	background colour, an initial canvas), re-read the older tests that assume the
319	old start.
320	
321	A bounds guard can be unreachable through the public API. TinyGL's clipper
322	keeps a line inside the view volume and its viewport maps that to at most pixel
323	63.5, so two of the four guards in the smooth-line plot survived mutation until
324	a test used a viewport bigger than the canvas. Mutate each guard on its own
325	(a scratchpad script that edits, runs the suite and restores in `finally`),
326	and when one survives, find an input that reaches it or say it is defensive.
327	Wrapping bugs can also hide in what is stored, not what is drawn: a depth that
328	wrapped round only showed when a third fill was drawn afterwards.
329	
330	## Wrapping an xlockmore hack's init or draw
331	
332	Emptying `XSCREENSAVER_MODULE` (Blaster) fails: the hack includes
333	`xlockmore.h`, which has no include guard and defines it again. Rename the
334	hack's tables instead (`#define pipes_xscreensaver_function_table
335	pipes_upstream_xscreensaver_table`, the same for `_xlockmore_function_table`),
336	include the hack, `#undef` both, define the wrappers, then
337	`#define draw_pipes pipes_draw_no_fade` and call
338	`XSCREENSAVER_MODULE_2("Pipes", pipes, pipes)`. See `hacks/pipes_gl.c`.
339	
340	## Background colour
341	
342	The runner paints the canvas in the hack's `background` resource before `init`,
343	as `screenhack.c` paints the window. Substrate (`.background: white`) depends
344	on it. Every earlier hack asks for black or nothing.
345	
346	## Skipping a hack
347	
348	Threads and shared memory are not worth porting. Record the name and the
349	reason in `tools/failed_ports.txt` (`name: reason`); the scorer marks it as
350	abandoned. Xft text used to be on this list; it is not now (see "Xft text").
351	
352	## Xft text
353	
354	A hack that draws with Xft (`XftDrawStringUtf8`, `load_xft_font_retry`) needs
355	the stand-in in `x11shim/xft.h`. Its font is Special Elite, rasterised at build
356	time into pixel-coverage tables (`firmware/font_atlas.py`, which runs
357	`tools/make_font_atlas.py` on the TTF in `firmware/assets/fonts/`), and
358	`main.cpp` installs it with `xshim_set_font`. Only ASCII has glyphs: anything
359	else draws as `?`. The family in a font name is ignored and the baked size
360	nearest the number is used, so to change a hack's text size override its font
361	resource (XJack's `XJACK_FONT_PX`) and bake the size in `font_atlas.py`.
362	
363	Our `screenhack.h` does not include `xft.h`, because that would change what
364	every hack sees. Build the hack through a wrapper that includes it first
365	(`hacks/xjack_xft.c`), and exclude the original from all three
366	`build_src_filter` lines. XJack's wrapper shows two things an Xft hack may
367	need from `screenhack.c`: the window background set from the `background`
368	resource (`XClearWindow` otherwise clears to black), and a reshape after
369	init. Tests that run the hack install `test_font.h`'s blocky font, so a
370	pinned hash does not follow FreeType; with no font installed the shim gives a
371	blank one, so a test that replays every hack does not abort.
372	
373	## Worktree setup
374	
375	A fresh worktree lacks the ignored `vendor/`, `.venv/` and `.platformio/`:
376	symlink them from the main checkout. They show as untracked, so `git add`
377	named paths, never `-A`. Adding them to `.git/info/exclude` changes state shared
378	with every worktree: ask Rod first.
379	
380	A worktree session refuses `source`, `$VAR` in a command and `&&` chains with a
381	computed path. Run plain commands with literal paths, for example
382	`PLATFORMIO_CORE_DIR=<worktree>/.platformio ../.venv/bin/pio test -e native`.
383	
384	## Device capture
385	
386	- Pin the hack with `-DSTART_HACK=\"name\"` and add `-DROTATE_SECONDS=0`, or the
387	  board rotates to the next hack after 90 s.
388	- Send upload output to a file, never through `head`, and look for "Hash of
389	  data verified".
390	- Capture 150 s or more of serial in the background, longer to see a restart.
391	  Read `step`, `push`, `wait`, heap and PSRAM, and any "Stack canary".
392	- Compare with a baseline from the same build, not with old rows: pushes became
393	  41-45 ms on every hack after the byte-order fix, against 31 ms before (#23).
394	- Pinning a frame hash: set the new hack's `kBaseline` entry to `1`, run
395	  `pio test -f test_hacks`, read `Was N` in the failure and convert with
396	  `python3 -c "print('0x%016xull' % N)"`. Pin only after looking at the frame
397	  (and never type the hex by hand: one was wrong).
398	- Showing Rod a hack: flash `-DSTART_HACK=\"first\" -DROTATE_SECONDS=25` with
399	  `XS_LOGO=...` so the new ones come up in order, then tell him which, and that
400	  the button steps backwards (from Pyro it wraps to the last hack).

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: copies data files the GL hacks include from
vendor/ into the build directory, where the wrappers find them. They carry no
licence text of their own, so they are never committed (see
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)."""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

repo = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"]).parent  # noqa: F821
sys.path.insert(0, str(repo / "tools"))
import xs_vendor

glx = xs_vendor.upstream(repo) / "hacks" / "glx"
generated = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated"  # noqa: F821

for name in ("curlicue.h", "graphstat.h"):
    source = glx / name
    target = generated / name
    if not source.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"{source} is missing: run `uv run tools/fetch_xscreensaver.py`")
    data = source.read_bytes()
    if not target.exists() or target.read_bytes() != data:
        generated.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_bytes(data)

env.Append(CPPPATH=[str(generated)])  # noqa: F821

        f"/* Generated by tools/make_logo_blob.py from {source}; do not edit.\n"
        " * Despite the name (maze.c asks for a PNG), this is the raw blob\n"
        " * described in ximage-loader.h. */\n"
        f"#ifndef {guard}\n"
        f"#define {guard}\n"
        f"static const unsigned char {name}[] = {{\n"
        f"{body}\n"
        "};\n"
        "#endif\n"
    )


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    from PIL import Image

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=(__doc__ or "").split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("image")
    parser.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="C array name")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", required=True)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--size",
        type=int,
        help="shrink to fit this many pixels square, keeping the aspect ratio "
        "(never enlarges)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--deflate", action="store_true", help='write the compressed "565Z" form'
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    image = Image.open(args.image).convert("RGBA")
    if args.size:
        image.thumbnail((args.size, args.size), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    blob = build_blob(image.width, image.height, image.tobytes())
    if args.deflate:
        blob = deflate_blob(blob)

    # Left alone when unchanged, so an unchanged logo does not rebuild.
    output = Path(args.output)
    text = c_header(args.name, blob, Path(args.image).name)
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not output.exists() or output.read_text() != text:
        output.write_text(text)
    print(f"{args.output}: {image.width}x{image.height}, {len(blob)} bytes")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

Rod, Phosphor is doable but not small. I stopped at the scoping stage and haven't written any code. The port is an L-rated job, but L here comes from one cluster of 1-bit bitmap gaps, not from a pile of missing calls.

**What I found**
- **Already in the shim:**
  - `textclient.h`, `X11/Intrinsic.h` and the Xft stand-in all exist.
  - Cursor blink won't run, because Xt timers never fire. The cursor just stays on.
- **Copy as-is:** `ansi-tty.c` and `ansi-tty.h` have the standard jwz licence, so they need a notices row.
- **Shim gaps to fill, test-first:**
  - `blurb.h`.
  - `utf8_encode` and `utf8_decode`, which `ansi-tty.c` uses.
  - A "565Z" blob of `6x10font.png`, committed as a small generated header like the logos.
- **The hard part is the glyph pipeline:** it assumes real 1-bit pixmaps. The shim can't `XDrawLine` into a bitmap, `XGetImage` a bitmap, or `XPutImage` onto one.
- **My plan for that:** a `phosphor_*.c` wrapper that leaves `phosphor.c` byte-identical. It replaces `capture_font_bits` with a version built from `image_data_to_ximage`, and routes `XDrawLine` on a bitmap to a rectangle fill. That keeps the change out of the shared shim.
- **Settings I'd change:**
  - The default scale of 6 gives only a 12×7 grid on 466 px, so I'd override it to about 3 (roughly 25×15).
  - `cache` must be off. At that scale the per-glyph fade cache is around 20 MB, against 8 MB of PSRAM.
- **Text source:** with no pty on the board, the wrapper needs its own `textclient`. It would be a short canned, deterministic terminal session using a few ANSI sequences, which also makes it testable. The shared `textclient.h` stays as it is, so XMatrix is untouched.
- **Open risk:** the speed. Every fading cell is redrawn every frame, so I'd expect a few hundred cell redraws a frame. I won't know the fps until it runs.

**Two things I need from you**
1. There's no Linear ticket for Phosphor (I searched the ARS team). AGENTS.md says to ask before working untracked: shall I file one?
2. Are you happy with the wrapper approach? It leaves the shared shim and `textclient.h` alone, but it means a canned text session instead of real `xscreensaver-text` output.

I'm on branch `wip/phosphor-port` with nothing changed. Once you've answered, I'll start with the failing registry test.
File a ticket and go with the wrapper approach

# Linear tracking

Moved verbatim from AGENTS.md.

## Filing issues

- Every issue gets the `stopwatch-screensaver` label (in the `Repo` group) and exactly
  one label from the `Work Type` group. The group is single-select, so
  pick the one that fits best (see below).
- Always set a priority (Urgent, High, Medium, Low). Never leave it at
  "No priority".
- Link the draft trail or spec section if one exists. Copy the body from
  `entire trail show N --json`; `entire trail list --json` returns empty
  bodies.

## Choosing a Work Type

| Label         | Use it for                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `Bug`         | Fixing something that isn't operating correctly. |
| `Feature`     | Adding new functionality to the app.             |
| `Enhancement` | Improving existing functionality.                |
| `Performance` | Improving the performance of code.               |
| `Chore`       | Maintenance, tooling and documentation work.     |

Several of these can fit one ticket. Decide by asking these in order and
taking the first yes:

1. Does the app do something other than what was intended? `Bug`, even if
   the symptom is slowness or the fix is a refactor.
1. Is the behaviour right, but too slow or heavy, and is speed or
   resource use the point of the work? `Performance`.
1. Does it give the user a capability they did not have? `Feature`.
1. Does it make a capability they already have better? `Enhancement`.
1. Does it change nothing a user would notice? `Chore`.

A ticket that bundles small, unrelated tidy-ups takes `Chore`. If the
bundle is mostly one other type, either split it or use that type.
Refactors, test additions, dependency bumps, build scripts, CI and
documentation are `Chore` unless they fix a defect.

## Status names

Use these exactly as Linear spells them: `Backlog`, `Todo`,
`In Progress`, `In Review`, `Done`, `Canceled`, `Duplicate`.
Feature, since it's a new hack. Filing it and moving it straight to In Progress, since I'm starting now.

- Own canned, deterministic text source (a few ANSI sequences) in place of `xscreensaver-text`; no pty on the board.
- Override `phosphorScale` to about 3 (about 25x15 grid on 466 px) and `cache` off (the fade cache would be about 20 MB against 8 MB PSRAM).

GUARD = "#ifdef HAVE_AFTER_DARK_TOASTERS\n"


def _guard_in(text: str, start: str, end: str) -> int:
    """Index of GUARD between `start` and `end`, or -1."""
    a = text.find(start)
    b = text.find(end, a)
    if a < 0 or b < 0:
        return -1
    return text.find(GUARD, a, b)


def wire(
    root: Path,
    name: str,
    cls: str,
    copyright_text: str,
    notice: str = "jwz permission notice (above)",
    xlockmore: bool = False,
    glx: bool = False,
) -> None:
    src = root / UPSTREAM / "hacks" / ("glx" if glx else "") / f"{name}.c"
    if not src.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(src)
    dst = root / "firmware" / "src" / "hacks" / name / f"{name}.c"
    registry = root / "firmware" / "src" / "hacks" / "registry.c"
    tests = root / "firmware" / "test" / "test_hacks" / "test_hacks.c"
    notices = root / "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md"

    reg = registry.read_text()
    if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(name)}_hack\b", reg):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} is already in registry.c")
    if xlockmore:
        decl = f'XLOCKMORE_HACK({name}, "{cls}");\n'
    else:
        decl = f"extern const HackEntry {name}_hack;\n"
    reg = _insert_before(reg, "const HackEntry *const g_hacks[]", decl + "\n")
    g = _guard_in(reg, "g_hacks[] = {", "};")
    if g >= 0:
        reg = reg[:g] + f"    &{name}_hack,\n" + reg[g:]
    else:
        reg, n = re.subn(
            r"    &(\w+)_hack\};", rf"    &\1_hack,\n    &{name}_hack}};", reg, count=1
        )
        if n != 1:
            raise ValueError("cannot find the end of g_hacks[]")

    t = tests.read_text()
    g = _guard_in(t, "expected[] = {", "const int n = sizeof(expected)")
    if g >= 0:
        t = t[:g] + f'                                         "{cls}",\n' + t[g:]
    else:
        t, n = re.subn(
            r'"\};\n  const int n = sizeof\(expected\)',
            f'",\n                                         "{cls}"}};\n  const int n = sizeof(expected)',
            t,
            count=1,
        )
        if n != 1:
            raise ValueError("cannot find the expected list in test_hacks.c")
    g = _guard_in(
        t, "kBaseline[] = {", "void test_frames_of_every_hack_but_maze_match_main"
    )
    if g >= 0:
        t = t[:g] + f"    0, /* {cls}: not yet pinned */\n" + t[g:]
    else:
        t, n = re.subn(
            r"(\};\n\nvoid test_frames_of_every_hack_but_maze_match_main)",
            f"    0, /* {cls}: not yet pinned */\n\\1",
            t,
            count=1,
        )
        if n != 1:
            raise ValueError("cannot find kBaseline in test_hacks.c")
    leak = (
        f"void test_{name}_stops_do_not_leak(void) {{\n"
        f'  check_restarts_and_stops_do_not_leak("{cls}", {1 if xlockmore else 0});\n'
        "}\n\n"
    )
    t = _insert_before(t, "int main(void) {\n  UNITY_BEGIN();", leak)
    t = _insert_before(
        t,
        "  RUN_TEST(test_gears_stack_use_on_the_host_has_not_run_away);\n",
        f"  RUN_TEST(test_{name}_stops_do_not_leak);\n",
    )

    n_text = notices.read_text()
    rows = list(re.finditer(r"\| `firmware/src/hacks/[^\n]*\n", n_text))
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("no hack rows in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md")
    row = f"| `firmware/src/hacks/{name}/{name}.c` | {copyright_text} | {notice} |\n"
    n_text = n_text[: rows[-1].end()] + row + n_text[rows[-1].end() :]

    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy(src, dst)
    registry.write_text(reg)
    tests.write_text(t)
    notices.write_text(n_text)


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=(__doc__ or "").split("\n\n")[0])
    p.add_argument("name")
    p.add_argument("cls", metavar="Class")
    p.add_argument("copyright", metavar="copyright")
    p.add_argument("--notice", default="jwz permission notice (above)")
    p.add_argument("--xlockmore", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--glx", action="store_true", help="the source is under hacks/glx/")
    a = p.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        wire(ROOT, a.name, a.cls, a.copyright, a.notice, a.xlockmore, a.glx)
    except (ValueError, FileNotFoundError) as e:
        print(f"wire_hack: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"wired {a.name} ({a.cls}); now fill the shim gaps and run `pio run -e dump`")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

Maze draws the xscreensaver logo inside its maze. The logo data in
`logo-50_png.h` is `utils/images/logo-50.gif` from xscreensaver 6.17,
re-encoded as 50 by 50 RGB565 pixels and a transparency mask, without

Going well, with the port working on the host. The commit is still running its pre-commit hooks and hasn't landed yet. The files are staged and `HEAD` is unchanged.

**Working**
- Phosphor runs on the host: a green terminal session with the glow and fade, scale 3, a 25×15 grid, and text kept inside the round bezel's visible area.
- Upstream `phosphor.c` and `ansi-tty` are byte-identical copies, with notices rows added, including one for the font.
- The shim now has bitmap `XDrawLine`, `XGetImage`, `XPutImage` and `XCopyPlane`, plus `utf8_encode`/`utf8_decode` and `blurb.h`. The shim tests pass, 293 plus the new ones.
- The leak test passes: `leaks` reports 0 bytes after I fixed upstream's leaks in the wrapper.

**Caught along the way**
- A shared clip-mask change to `XFillRectangle` moved Bubbles' and Pacman's pinned frames. I made it Phosphor-only through the wrapper, and both are back to their pins.
- The full `test_hacks` run (5.5 minutes) now fails only on Phosphor's own hash. I've since pinned it from the frame I viewed, but I haven't re-run the suite with that pin.

**Next**
1. Let the commit land.
2. Run the mutation checks. The script is written and covers 14 shim mutants.
3. Re-run the full suite.
4. Build for the device and, since you've said I can, flash it and read fps and heap.

I haven't built for the device or measured speed yet. The risk is that every fading cell redraws each frame.
Try the commit again. I'd rebooted my computer, so my signing key wasn't in my ssh-agent. It should complete quickly now.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/rod/build/stopwatch-screensaver/.claude/skills/device-run

# Flashing and measuring on the device

Moved verbatim from AGENTS.md.

- `pio run -e stopwatch`: build for the device. Add `-t upload` to flash.
  The device starts on a random hack; to pin one while examining it, prefix
  `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS='-DSTART_HACK=\"galaxy\"'` (a name from `g_hacks[]`,
  any case; an unknown name falls back to random and logs it). Rebuild without
  it afterwards, since the define sticks to the build. Unescaped quotes fail
  with "error: 'truchet' was not declared in this scope".
  It rotates to the next hack every 90 s (a button press restarts the count);
  `-DROTATE_SECONDS=5` shortens that for leak testing and `=0` turns it off. A
  pinned build still rotates, so add `=0` to measure one hack.
  The log prints `rotate -> <hack> heap= psram=` at each change. Combine flags
  in one `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS` string.
  `-DBADGE_NAME=\"Rod\ B.\"` sets the name badge text (default "Rod" over
  "Begbie"; `\n` starts a new line). Check a
  flag reached the binary with
  `strings -a -n 3 .pio/build/stopwatch/firmware.elf | grep -c '^Rod B\.$'`:
  plain `strings` skips anything under 4 characters.
  `-DQR_URL=\"https://example.com\"` sets the QR overlay's target (default the
  LinkedIn profile). Check it reached the binary with
  `strings -a .pio/build/stopwatch/firmware.elf | grep -c 'example.com'`.
  In a worktree session the harness refuses backslash-escaped flag values and
  `$(cat file)`. Use `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS="'-DBADGE_NAME=\"Rod B.\"'
  '-DSTART_HACK=\"gears\"' -DROTATE_SECONDS=0"` with `.venv/bin/pio run -d
  firmware -e stopwatch -t upload` from the worktree root.
- Serial log: `.venv/bin/python -I tools/serial_capture.py <out-file>
  <seconds> [port]` reads `/dev/cu.usbmodem112401` at 115200 into a file and
  reopens the port when it goes away. Run it in the background with absolute
  paths, since background shells ignore `cd`. Lines to read:
  `run <hack> fps= step= push= sync= wait= rows=` (ms per frame in the hack,
  the push, the wait for the panel's TE edge before a synced push (only
  Unknown Pleasures; not counted in `push=`) and the wait; mean canvas rows
  sent per frame, 466 being a full push,
  though overlay redraws made while waiting can push it higher)
  and `switch -> <hack> press_waited=`. An empty capture, or "Device not
  configured", means the USB port went away and came back (a flash, a crash):
  reopen it in a loop. Opening the port resets the board
  (`rst:0x15 USB_UART_CHIP_RESET`, even with DTR/RTS held low): the overlay
  returns to nothing and a random hack starts. To measure one hack, flash a
  pinned build (`START_HACK` plus `ROTATE_SECONDS=0`), start the capture, then
  tap during it: the early windows are the baseline, the later ones have the
  overlay.
  `serial_capture.py` sets `dtr` and `rts` to False on an unopened
  `serial.Serial()` before `open()`, as any script of your own must: a reopen
  loop without that once parked the chip in its bootloader
  (`boot:0x3 ... waiting for download`, screen frozen). Recover, or reset just
  before a capture to log from boot (a hack's `fprintf(stderr)` reaches the
  log), with `.venv/bin/python .platformio/packages/tool-esptoolpy/esptool.py
  --chip esp32s3 --port /dev/cu.usbmodem112401 --after hard_reset read_mac`.
- Flash with `pio run -e stopwatch -t upload > file 2>&1`, never piped through
  `head`, and check for "Hash of data verified". The button steps backwards
  (Pyro, then Lightning, then Drift...). Work out how long a restart takes
  from the hack's cycle count times its frame time (Substrate: 10,000 cycles
  at about 160 ms is 27 minutes) and capture that long, with rotation off.
- `ad-flyingtoasters` force flags (add to `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS`):
  `-DAD_TOASTERS_ART=0|1` (0 is 1-bit, 1 is colour) and
  `-DAD_TOASTERS_DONENESS=0|1|2` (light, medium, dark) and
  `-DAD_TOASTERS_SCALE=1|2` (2 is the default, with 6 flyers; 1 is the
  original size, with 10); a number outside those is an `#error`. It logs
  `ad-flyingtoasters: <art>, doneness=<level>` to stderr at start.
- To see where a GL hack's frame goes, add `-DGL_PROFILE`: a `glprof` line
  follows each `run` line with time per stage (clear, list, vertex, shade,
  tri, fill, point, line; nested, so vertex includes tri and fill). Time left
  over is the hack's own code. To compare builds, `.venv/bin/python -I
  tools/ab_flash.py --hack Gears --seconds 60 --rounds 2 --out <dir>
  "a=-DGL_PROFILE" "b=-DGL_PROFILE -DFOO"` builds each variant pinned, flashes
  them in turn and tabulates the windows. It flashes: run it only with Rod's
  go-ahead. It builds each hack's variants from the working tree when that
  hack's turn starts, so leave `src/` and `tools/tinygl_patch.py` alone until
  the last hack has built. It compares flag variants of one tree: to A/B a
  change, put it behind a temporary `-D` switch (as `-DPUSH_NO_DISC` does).
  It takes one `--hack` per run: loop several from a scratchpad script run
  with `run_in_background`, and `touch` a done file at the end.
- `-DDCACHE_LINE32` keeps the SDK's 32-byte data-cache lines for every hack
  (the default is 64 bytes, see `device-display.md`), so it is the A side of an
  `ab_flash` comparison. `-DPSRAM_BENCH` boots into `diag/psram_bench.h`
  instead of the runner and prints cost per cache miss, sequential rates and a
  working-set sweep; `-DPSRAM_BENCH_VARIANT=0..3` picks the line size and
  prefetch setting.
- `esptool` reads of the 16 MB flash need `--baud 921600` (about 3.5 minutes)
  and show no progress when piped.
- The port name changes with the USB socket the board is plugged into
  (`/dev/cu.usbmodem112401` became `/dev/cu.usbmodem101` on 2026-10-14). When
  it is missing, find the board without touching it:
  `ioreg -p IOUSB -l -w0 | grep -E "\+-o|idVendor|idProduct|USB Product
  Name|USB Serial Number"` lists USB devices, and
  `ioreg -r -c IOSerialBSDClient -l | grep IOCalloutDevice` lists the serial
  ports. The StopWatch is the "USB JTAG/serial debug unit" from Espressif
  (`idVendor` 12346, `idProduct` 4097). Its USB serial number is its MAC:
  Rod's board is `28:84:85:43:B2:70`, so check that before flashing a port
  you have not used before. Pass `--upload-port <port>` to `pio run -t upload`
  and read the same port for the serial log, and leave `platformio.ini`'s
  `upload_port` alone. Still ask Rod before each flash. The auto-mode
  classifier refused a flash to an overridden port once: give Rod the command
  to run with `!`.
- Another session may be using the board. Before flashing, run `lsof
  /dev/cu.usbmodem112401`: a "multiple access on port" upload error was
  another session's serial capture, and esptool's connect resets the board
  under it. Ask Rod before flashing over someone else's run.
- PlatformIO cleans the build directory, image and all, when
  `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS` changes: an `-t nobuild -t upload` with other flags
  finds no `firmware.bin`. To keep several images, give each its own
  `PLATFORMIO_BUILD_DIR` (the build scripts all use `$BUILD_DIR`).
- Read `push=` from a hack's second 5 s window on: the name overlay is stamped
  inside the push timing while it shows, so the first window reads high.
- `heap=` and `psram=` are the reading at the end of a window, not a minimum:
  a hack with a long pause and nothing held in it (Celtic's 5 s `*delay2`)
  reads idle in every window. Sample while it works, or read `rotate ->`.
- Report a hack's lowest `fps=` window as well as its mean. HexTrail's step
  grows over a 65 s cycle: mean 15.3, worst window 10.8, and Rod saw an earlier
  build sag under 10 fps before the rotation moved on. Capture a full cycle and
  say which build the board holds when you stop.
- A boot is deterministic (same hack, layout and windows), so to compare two
  builds flash them alternately and compare window by window; one reading in
  three captures was an unexplained outlier, so never trust a single pair.
- Leak-testing with `-DROTATE_SECONDS=5`: internal heap falls about 26 KB
  during the first lap and then stays flat. Compare lap 2 with lap 3, not
  with lap 1. PSRAM should match exactly on every visit.
- To prove a device-only path the host cannot run (the ROM's `tinfl`), add a
  temporary `#ifdef` block after `printStats("boot")` in `main.cpp` that logs
  a checksum, compare it with one computed in Python, then `git checkout
  firmware/src/main.cpp` before pushing.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/rod/.claude/skills/markdown

# GitHub Flavored Markdown Generation

**Version:** 1.2.1

Generate GFM that passes markdownlint validation with zero violations.

## Core Principles

### 1. Blank Lines Are Mandatory

- Before/after ALL lists (MD032)
- Before/after ALL headings except document start (MD022)
- Before/after ALL code blocks (MD031)
- Between ALL block-level elements

### 2. Consistency Required

- Use `-` for lists
- Use `#` for headings (ATX)
- Regular spaces only—never tabs/nbsp

### 3. Structure Matters

- Heading hierarchy: 1→2→3 (not 1→3)
- ONE H1 per document
- Files end with one newline
- Lines under 80 chars

### 4. Invisible Characters Matter

- Use ONLY regular spaces (U+0020)
- Never non-breaking spaces (U+00A0,  )
- Never tabs
- UTF-8 encoding

## Pre-Generation Checklist

- [ ] Where will lists/headings/code appear?
- [ ] Heading levels verified (1→2→3)?
- [ ] Using `-` for all lists?
- [ ] Code languages specified?
- [ ] Lines under 80 chars?
- [ ] Line breaks needed? (two trailing spaces)
- [ ] Using regular spaces only?
- [ ] URLs wrapped in `<>` or `[]`?
- [ ] Document starts with H1?
- [ ] Ordered lists use `1.` for all items?
- [ ] File ends with single newline?
- [ ] Tables use consistent spacing?

## Essential Rules

### Lists (MD032, MD004)

```markdown
Text before.

- Item one
- Item two

Text after.
```

### Headings (MD001, MD022)

```markdown
Text.

## Heading

Content.
```

### Code Blocks (MD031, MD040)

````markdown
Text.

```python
code()
```

Text.
````

**Nested Fences:** When showing markdown examples that contain code blocks,
use **one more backtick** than the deepest level:

- Three backticks (` ``` `): Regular code
- Four backticks (` ```` `): Markdown examples with code
- Five backticks (` ````` `): Nested markdown examples

`````markdown
````markdown
# Example

```bash
command
```

````
`````

### Line Length (MD013)

Break long lines at natural points. Use reference-style links for long URLs.

### URLs and Email (MD034)

Wrap bare URLs and emails:

```markdown
Wrong: https://example.com
Right: <https://example.com>
Right: [link](https://example.com)

Wrong: user@example.com
Right: <user@example.com>
```

### Document Structure (MD041)

Start with H1 (or front matter then H1):

```markdown
# Document Title

First paragraph.
```

### Ordered Lists (MD029)

Use `1.` for all items:

```markdown
1. First
1. Second
1. Third
```

### File Endings (MD047)

End with single newline:

```text
Last content line.
[single newline]
[EOF]
```

### Table Column Style (MD060)

Use consistent spacing in tables. Three styles:

**Compact (recommended):** `| cell |` - single space around content

```markdown
| Header 1 | Header 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Data | More data |
```

**Aligned:** Pipes vertically aligned with padding

**Tight:** `|cell|` - no spaces

Pick ONE style per document. Compact is preferred.

### Character Encoding

**Detection:** View → Render Whitespace in VS Code

**Fix:** Find `\u00A0` → Replace with space

**Critical for AI:** Two trailing spaces = intentional line breaks. Do NOT
remove them.

## Critical Error Patterns

### 1. List Without Blank Lines

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD032 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
Text:
- Item
Text.
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD032 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
Text:

- Item

Text.
```

### 2. Heading Without Blank Lines

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD022 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
Text.
## Head
Text.
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD022 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
Text.

## Head

Text.
```

### 3. Code Without Blanks/Language

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD031 MD040 -->

**Wrong:**

````markdown
Text:
```
code
```
Text.
````

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD031 MD040 -->

**Right:**

````markdown
Text:

```python

```

Text.
````

### 4. Inconsistent Markers

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD004 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
- Item
* Item
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD004 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
- Item
- Item
```

### 5. Skipping Levels

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD001 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
# Title

### Sub (skipped H2)
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD001 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
# Title

## Section

### Sub
```

## Post-Generation Validation

1. Lists have blank lines before/after
2. Headings have blank lines before/after
3. Code has blank lines before/after
4. Heading progression: 1→2→3→4
5. All lists use `-`
6. All code has language
7. Lines under 80 chars

10. Ordered lists use `1.`
11. File ends with one newline

13. Only regular spaces (no nbsp/tabs)
14. Tables use consistent column spacing

## Mental Model

Markdown is **blocks with mandatory spacing:**

```text
[Text Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Heading Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[List Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Code Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Text Block]
[EOF]
```

Every block transition = blank line required.

## Common Languages

**Programming:** `python` `javascript` `java` `c` `cpp` `go` `rust` `ruby`
`php` `swift` `kotlin` `typescript`

**Shell:** `bash` `sh` `powershell` `cmd` `zsh`

**Markup:** `html` `css` `xml` `json` `yaml` `toml` `markdown`

**Database:** `sql` `postgresql` `mysql`

**Other:** `text` `diff` `log`

## Validation

```bash
markdownlint filename.md
```

Goal: Zero errors/warnings.

## Additional Resources

See bundled references:

- `references/complete-rules.md` - Full rule catalog
- `references/edge-cases.md` - Platform quirks
- `references/examples.md` - Detailed examples

## Remember

Most common: Missing blank lines around lists/headings/code.

**Two trailing spaces:** Intentional line breaks. Do NOT remove.

When in doubt:

1. Add blank lines before/after blocks
2. Use `-` for lists
3. Use `#` for headings
4. Specify code language
5. Increment headings by one
6. Use regular spaces only
7. Two trailing spaces = line break

Phosphor is ported and running on the board, pinned with rotation off, so it should be on screen now. I'd like you to look at it before I open the PR.

**Please check:**
- Is the text legible on the round panel? It is a canned boot log, "Nobody asked for a glass terminal on a stopwatch.", loops about every 14 s, and is kept inside the circle's visible columns.
- Is scale 3 (a 25×15 grid) the right size? Scale 4 gives bigger letters on a 19×11 grid.
- Does the phosphor glow and fade look right when the screen clears?

**Where it stands**
- **Host:** the full native suite passes (899 of 899) and the Python tests pass (652 passed, 1 skipped). `check_notices` is clean.
- **Device:** 11.0–17.8 fps (mean 16.0), paced by its own 50 ms delay. The dips to 11–12 fps come from 20–36 ms steps when the whole screen fades after a clear. Free PSRAM was flat over 16 windows, with no stack canary or reboot lines. I haven't done a rotation soak yet.
- **Tests:** I mutation-checked the new shim code (all killed, after adding one test for a survivor). I did the same for the wrapper's clipped fill and its leak fixes (all killed).
- **Branch:** everything is committed on `feature/ARS-58-phosphor` in 4 commits, ending at c871a6b. It isn't pushed, and there is no PR yet.

**One thing to know about the approach**
I put the missing bitmap operations in the shim itself: lines, `XGetImage`, `XPutImage` and `XCopyPlane` on bitmaps. That is more than the wrapper-only approach we agreed. Making the shared `XFillRectangle` honour clip masks moved Bubbles' and Pacman's pinned frames, so that one fill lives only in Phosphor's wrapper. If you'd rather I keep the bitmap operations out of the shared shim too, say so and I'll move them.

**Next, once you've looked**
1. Open the draft PR via `deliver-branch` and move ARS-58 to In Review.
2. Re-flash a plain rotating build. The board stays pinned to Phosphor until I do.

Scale 3 looks good as does the phosphor glow.  Can you maybe find some public domain poetry (The Raven? This Is Just To Say? This Be The Verse?  Stuff like that) and then pick them at random to "cat" in the terminal?

Quick copyright check before I start, since only public-domain poems can go in the repo (in the US, published 1930 or earlier):

- **The Raven** (Poe) is fine.
- **This Is Just To Say** is Williams, 1934, and **This Be The Verse** is Larkin, 1971, so both are still in copyright. I'll use Williams's **The Red Wheelbarrow** instead. It was published in 1923 and has been public domain since 2019.
- I'll add short Frost, Shelley, Dickinson and Blake poems, taking the text from a source rather than my memory.

cat > tools/make_phosphor_poems.py <<'EOF'
"""Turn firmware/assets/phosphor-poems.txt into the C header Phosphor's text
source reads.

Each poem becomes one string of terminal output: clear the screen, type a
`cat` command, then the poem word-wrapped to fit the part of the round panel
that shows (see the table below), inside a scroll region so a long poem
scrolls where it can be seen.

Run with: uv run tools/make_phosphor_poems.py
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SOURCE = ROOT / "firmware" / "assets" / "phosphor-poems.txt"
OUTPUT = ROOT / "firmware" / "src" / "hacks" / "phosphor_poems.h"

# At scale 3 the grid is 25 by 15 cells, and the circle shows columns 4 to 21
# on rows 2 to 13 (rows 0, 1 and 14 are mostly off the glass).
INDENT = 4
WIDTH = 18
HANGING = 2
FIRST_ROW = 2
LAST_ROW = 13
SCROLL_TOP = FIRST_ROW + 2  # the command line, then a gap

CLEAR = "\x1b[r\x1b[2J\x1b[H"


def wrap(line: str) -> list[str]:
    """Greedy word wrap: the first piece WIDTH wide, later ones HANGING
    narrower and indented by it. A word longer than the room is an error."""
    pieces: list[str] = []
    current = ""
    for word in line.split():
        room = WIDTH if not pieces else WIDTH - HANGING
        if len(word) > room:
            raise ValueError(f"{word!r} is wider than {room} columns")
        if current and len(current) + 1 + len(word) <= room:
            current += " " + word
        else:
            if current:
                pieces.append(current)
            current = word
            room = WIDTH - HANGING
    pieces.append(current)
    return [pieces[0]] + [" " * HANGING + p for p in pieces[1:]]


def parse(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[str]]]:
    """(file name, byline, lines) for each poem; a blank line is kept."""
    poems: list[tuple[str, str, list[str]]] = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        if raw.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if raw.startswith("== "):
            name, _, byline = raw[3:].partition("|")
            poems.append((name.strip(), byline.strip(), []))
        elif poems:
            poems[-1][2].append(raw.rstrip())
        elif raw.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"text before the first poem: {raw!r}")
    for name, byline, lines in poems:
        while lines and not lines[-1]:
            lines.pop()
        if not name or not byline or not lines:
            raise ValueError(f"poem {name!r} needs a name, a byline and lines")
        for line in [name, byline, *lines]:
            if not line.isascii():
                raise ValueError(f"{line!r} is not ASCII: the font has no glyphs for it")
    return poems


def render(name: str, byline: str, lines: list[str]) -> str:
    """The terminal output for one poem."""
    out = [CLEAR, "\r\n" * FIRST_ROW, " " * INDENT + f"> cat {name}\r\n"]
    out.append(f"\x1b[{SCROLL_TOP + 1};{LAST_ROW + 1}r")
    body: list[str] = []
    for line in lines:
        body.extend(wrap(line) if line else [""])
    body += ["", f"-- {byline}", "", "> _"]
    for i, line in enumerate(body):
        indent = INDENT if not line.startswith(" ") else INDENT
        out.append(" " * indent + line if line else "")
        if i + 1 < len(body):
            out.append("\r\n")
    return "".join(out)


def c_string(text: str) -> str:
    """A C string literal, split after each newline so the lines stay short."""
    chunks = text.split("\n")
    pieces = []
    for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks):
        piece = chunk + ("\n" if i + 1 < len(chunks) else "")
        if not piece:
            continue
        escaped = (
            piece.replace("\\", "\\\\")
            .replace('"', '\\"')
            .replace("\x1b", "\\033")
            .replace("\r", "\\r")
            .replace("\n", "\\n")
        )
        pieces.append(f'    "{escaped}"')
    return "\n".join(pieces)


def header(text: str) -> str:
    poems = parse(text)
    body = []
    for name, byline, lines in poems:
        body.append(f"    /* {name} */\n{c_string(render(name, byline, lines))},")
    entries = "\n".join(body)
    return (
        "/* Generated by tools/make_phosphor_poems.py from "
        "firmware/assets/phosphor-poems.txt; do not edit. */\n"
        "#ifndef PHOSPHOR_POEMS_H\n"
        "#define PHOSPHOR_POEMS_H\n\n"
        "static const char *const kPoems[] = {\n"
        f"{entries}\n"
        "};\n\n"
        "#define POEM_COUNT ((int)(sizeof kPoems / sizeof kPoems[0]))\n\n"
        "#endif\n"
    )


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    text = header(SOURCE.read_text())
    if not OUTPUT.exists() or OUTPUT.read_text() != text:
        OUTPUT.write_text(text)
    print(f"{OUTPUT.relative_to(ROOT)}: {len(parse(SOURCE.read_text()))} poems")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
EOF

content.text:
The poem version is working and is on the board now, pinned to Phosphor with rotation off. Each loop it picks one of seven poems and never repeats the last one.

**The poems**
- All seven were published before 1931, so they're public domain in the US: The Raven (first stanza), Ozymandias, Fire and Ice, Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening, The Red Wheelbarrow, The Tyger and Hope is the thing with feathers.
- The texts come from Wikisource's transcriptions of the first printings, and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists them.
- I used The Red Wheelbarrow instead of This Is Just To Say, because the latter is still in copyright. Williams's 1923 poem has been public domain since 2019.
- Original spellings are kept ("desart" in Ozymandias, "sieze" in The Tyger).

**What you'll see**
- Each loop starts with `> cat raven`, then the poem types out a character at a time.
- A long poem is shown in pages, ending in `--More--`, then the screen clears and the next page types. Scrolling smeared ghosts of the old text under the new, so I used pages instead.
- Lines are word-wrapped to 18 columns and kept to the rows and columns the round panel shows, so nothing sits in the clipped corners.

**Device numbers (22 windows over 120 s)**
- 13.0–17.6 fps (mean 16.2), paced by its own 50 ms delay.
- Steps are 1.4–22 ms. Free PSRAM is flat, with no stack canary or reboot lines.
- That's the same speed as before, and the same glow you approved.

**Tests**
- The full native suite passes: 909 of 909. The Python tests for the poem generator pass.
- I mutation-checked the poem selection, the page and pause handling, and the generator, and all mutants are killed. One extra test came out of that: the first run left three survivors, all about what happens when a page or poem ends. I moved that logic into `phosphor_text.h` so it can be tested directly, and all three are now killed.
- Everything is committed on `feature/ARS-58-phosphor` (6 commits, latest 0fdeb9a), not yet pushed.

**Your call:** please look at the screen and check the pages read well, especially the long ones (Ozymandias is 7 pages, Woods is 6). If it's good I'll:
1. Open the draft PR via `deliver-branch`, with ARS-58 moved to In Review.
2. Re-flash a plain rotating build, so the board isn't left pinned to Phosphor.
Try it without pages. I'd like to see what the performance is like with scrolling.  (Also, grab Wordworth's Daffodils and the Charge of the Light Brigade if you can.  And Rabbie Burns's mouse poem)
Two jobs here: build a scrolling variant to compare on the device, and add the three poems. Starting with fetching the poem texts.
The Maud edition of the Charge has an unusual five-stanza ending. I'd rather use the standard six-stanza text, so I'm fetching it from the anthology printing.
I have all three texts. Now the generator changes: a scroll mode alongside paging, bylines wrapped so "-- Wordsworth, 1815" doesn't run past the circle, and a build flag in the wrapper to choose.

I wandered lonely as a Cloud
That floats on high o'er Vales and Hills,
When all at once I saw a crowd,
A host of golden Daffodils;
Beside the Lake, beneath the trees,
Fluttering and dancing in the breeze.

Continuous as the stars that shine
And twinkle on the milky way,
They stretched in never-ending line
Along the margin of a bay:
Ten thousand saw I at a glance,
Tossing their heads in sprightly dance.

The waves beside them danced, but they
Out-did the sparkling waves in glee:--
A Poet could not but be gay
In such a jocund company:
I gazed--and gazed--but little thought
What wealth the shew to me had brought:

For oft when on my couch I lie
In vacant or in pensive mood,
They flash upon that inward eye
Which is the bliss of solitude,
And then my heart with pleasure fills,
And dances with the Daffodils.

== charge | Tennyson, 1854
Half a league, half a league,
Half a league onward,
All in the valley of Death
Rode the six hundred.
"Forward, the Light Brigade!
Charge for the guns!" he said:
Into the valley of Death
Rode the six hundred.

"Forward, the Light Brigade!"
Was there a man dismay'd?
Not tho' the soldier knew
Some one had blunder'd:
Theirs not to make reply,
Theirs not to reason why,
Theirs but to do and die:
Into the valley of Death
Rode the six hundred.

Cannon to right of them,
Cannon to left of them,
Cannon in front of them
Volley'd and thunder'd;
Storm'd at with shot and shell,
Boldly they rode and well,
Into the jaws of Death,
Into the mouth of Hell
Rode the six hundred.

Flash'd all their sabers bare,
Flash'd as they turn'd in air
Sab'ring the gunners there,
Charging an army, while
All the world wonder'd:
Plunged in the battery-smoke
Right thro' the line they broke;
Cossack and Russian
Reel'd from the saber-stroke
Shatter'd and sunder'd.
Then they rode back, but not
Not the six hundred.

Cannon to right of them,
Cannon to left of them,
Cannon behind them
Volleyed and thundered:
Stormed at with shot and shell,
While horse and hero fell,
They that had fought so well
Came through the jaws of death
Back from the mouth of hell,
All that was left of them--
Left of six hundred.

When can their glory fade?
Oh, the wild charge they made!
All the world wondered.
Honour the charge they made!
Honour the Light Brigade--
Noble six hundred!

== mouse | Burns, 1785
Wee, sleekit, cow'rin, tim'rous beastie,
O, what a panic's in thy breastie!
Thou need na start awa sae hasty,
Wi' bickering brattle!
I wad be laith to rin an' chase thee,
Wi' murd'ring pattle!

I'm truly sorry man's dominion
Has broken Nature's social union,
An' justifies that ill opinion,
Which makes thee startle,
At me, thy poor, earth-born companion,
An' fellow-mortal!

I doubt na, whiles, but thou may thieve;
What then? poor beastie, thou maun live!
A daimen-icker in a thrave
'S a sma' request:
I'll get a blessin wi' the lave,
And never miss't!

Thy wee bit housie, too, in ruin!
Its silly wa's the win's are strewin!
An' naething, now, to big a new ane,
O' foggage green;
An' bleak December's winds ensuin,
Baith snell an' keen!

Thou saw the fields laid bare an' waste,
An' weary winter comin fast,
An' cozie here, beneath the blast,
Thou thought to dwell,
Till crash! the cruel coulter past,
Out thro' thy cell.

That wee bit heap o' leaves an' stibble,
Has cost thee mony a weary nibble!
Now thou's turn'd out, for a' thy trouble,
But house or hald,
To thole the winter's sleety dribble,
An' cranreuch cauld!

But, Mousie, thou art no thy lane,
In proving foresight may be vain:
The best laid schemes o' mice an' men
Gang aft a-gley,
An' lea'e us nought but grief an' pain,
For promis'd joy.

Still thou art blest, compar'd wi' me!
The present only toucheth thee:
But, Och! I backward cast my e'e
On prospects drear!
An' forward, tho' I canna see,
I guess an' fear!

content.text:
Scrolling costs noticeably more than paging, so here is the comparison, with the scrolling build now on the board for you to watch.

| | Paged | Scrolling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fps | 13.0–17.6, mean 16.2 | 10.0–17.6, mean 13.6 |
| Step | 1.4–22 ms | 1.6–44.8 ms (mean 21.8) |
| Push | 0.5–3.2 ms | 0.6–9.7 ms (mean 4.6) |
| Rows pushed per frame | about 48 | 30–281 (mean 150) |

- **Why it costs more:** every scroll moves the whole text block up a row, so every cell is redrawn at once and many rows get pushed. Paging only redraws at a clear.
- **What stays the same:** free PSRAM is flat, and there are no canary or reboot lines.
- **Dips:** scrolling drops to 10.0–11.8 fps in many windows. That's the worst case I've seen for this hack, and it's what you'd notice by eye as steadier or choppier typing.
- **Looks:** you'll also see the ghost afterimages on every scroll that made me switch to paging. If you like that smeared-phosphor look, that's a point for scrolling.

**New poems**
- **Added:** I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud (Wordsworth, 1815 text), The Charge of the Light Brigade (Tennyson) and To a Mouse (Burns). That makes ten.
- **Charge text:** I used the standard six-stanza version, from the 1904 *Poems That Every Child Should Know* anthology on Wikisource.
- **Length:** Charge and Mouse are long: about 2,700 characters each, or around two minutes of typing. In paged mode that is 14–15 pages.
- **Byline:** bylines now wrap, so "-- Wordsworth, 1815" doesn't run past the circle.

**How I built it**
- Both layouts are generated and committed: `phosphor_poems.h` for pages and `phosphor_poems_scroll.h` for scrolling.
- `-DPHOSPHOR_SCROLL` picks the scrolling one, and paged is still the default.
- The generator tests pass (21).

**Still running:** the `test_hacks` re-pin. With ten poems, seed 1 may now pick a different poem, so the pinned hash will change. I haven't committed this round yet.

**Your call:** which do you want as the default, paged (smoother) or scrolling (more authentic phosphor, but down to 10 fps at times)? Once you've said, I'll commit with the right default, add the notices entries for the three new poems, and open the PR.
Lovely.  Scrolling should be the default.  One last question: Would tehre be a way to make the cursor blink?  That's the only thing I'm missing in this

Scrolling becomes the default. On the cursor: yes, it can be done. Upstream blinks it with Xt timers, and the shim's timers never fire, so I'll give Phosphor's wrapper a tiny timer queue of its own, driven from the draw call. I'm checking how tests fake the clock first.
